title: A Colony for the Static Again
premise: Lior Almeida keeps the beacon of Station Meridian alive, a lonely post orbiting a colony ship that never launched, until a manifest lists a passenger who shouldn't exist: Lior's own name, dated forty years in the future. Investigating the impossible record pulls Lior into contact with the ship's dormant AI, which reveals the vessel holds two cryo-banks—one for the loyalists who built it, one for the dissidents it was built to exile—and a reactor countdown that will kill whoever sleeps through it. As Lior falls for Sefa, an engineer sent to erase the evidence and everyone attached to it, they must choose which half of humanity wakes. In the end, Lior falsifies the final manifest with both names merged into one identity, waking a mixed remnant while sacrificing their own berth, and the beacon finally goes dark on purpose.
about_author: Lena Fairweather is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one else answered. She writes quiet science fiction about people who maintain things the world has forgotten.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a routine beacon audit, Lior finds their own name on the manifest of the Meridian—a ship that never flew—dated decades ahead. The station AI stonewalls, and an unscheduled shuttle approaches carrying Sefa Voss, claiming to be a records inspector. The beat is unease: the invisible life Lior built begins cracking at its first seam.

chapters.title: Two Banks of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Sefa POVs. Sefa's real orders surface: purge the cryo-banks and erase witnesses. But touring the frozen decks together, they discover the two banks hold ideologically split populations, and the reactor countdown is already running. Falling for each other, each hides what they know. The beat is intimacy shadowed by betrayal.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, then shared. Ordered to trigger the purge, Sefa instead confesses everything; Lior must decide whether loyalty to the sleepers outweighs the truth that half were meant to die. They race to override the AI, which reveals it chose them both long ago as arbiters. The climax: Lior rewrites the manifest, merging identities to wake a mixed remnant, forfeiting their own place.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The pods open on schedule; the chosen sleepers wake to a station stripped of its secrets and a beacon gone deliberately silent. Sefa carries Lior's final log entry to the survivors—an admission of love and of the lie that saved them. The beat is bittersweet resolution: truth survives, but only because someone loved enough to bury themselves inside it.
